finding.claim: DELETE /projects/:id calls authorized(), which returns a boolean, but ignores the result. Any authenticated user can delete any project regardless of ownership.
finding.source: Authenticated user's request DELETE /projects/:id with another user's project id (req.params.id)

trace.note: project fetched by id from the store with no owner scoping
authorized(req.user, project) is a bare statement; its boolean return is discarded and nothing is thrown
authorized() only returns true/false and never throws

finding.guards_checked: authorized() is the non-throwing variant, and the result is not used in an if. The sibling PUT route correctly uses the throwing authorize(). No other middleware is visible in this file; req.user and req.store are assumed to be set upstream. A nonexistent id leaves project undefined, so project.id throws a TypeError, which is not an authorization bypass.

verdict.guard_found: authorized() at api.js:12-14 only returns a boolean and never throws; its result is discarded at api.js:18. The throwing authorize() is used only on the PUT route (api.js:25). No other middleware is visible in this file.
verdict.reason: api.js:18 calls authorized() as a bare statement, so its false result is dropped and api.js:19 deletes the project for any authenticated user, whereas the PUT route at api.js:25 correctly uses the throwing authorize().
